bianzhong E55: Object Type A Chinese set of tuned bells hung on a rack and struck to sound. Scope E55: Note Type
musical instrument E55: Use Type
The Bianzhong of Marquis Yi of Zeng, or Zenghouyi Bells, is the name given to an ancient musical instrument made of bells (called bianzhong) unearthed in 1978 in the Tomb of Marquis Yi of Zeng in Leigudun Community, Nanjiao Subdistrict, Zengdu District, Suizhou (then "Sui County"), Hubei Province, China. The bianzhong were made in 433 B.C. Statement E55: Note Type
The instrument is a single functional aggregate: 64 bells hung on two sets of wooden racks. The bells are hung at three levels and are divided into eight groups: 19 bells in three groups at the top level, 33 bells in three groups in the middle level, and 12 bells in two groups at the bottom level. The two racks are perpendicular to each other. Description E55: Note Type
Each bell can play two tones with three degrees' interval between them. The tonal range is from C2 to D7. In the middle area of the tonal range the instrument can play all twelve half tones. Sound E55: Note Type
